opening_message:
Ticket 1: Donna Ball (employee ID E024) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E024.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin is only for the role that owns the system, so write is the maximum here. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB lists E024 as a contractor with basic training (HR note said full-time, but Security DB is authoritative for employment type). Contractors with basic training max out at read. Requested write exceeds max, so recommend granting read.
reason: Security records (authoritative for employment type) list E024 as a contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors max out at read unless they have advanced security training, which E024 does not. The requested write exceeds the maximum, so grant the maximum allowed level: read.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee: Donna Ball (E024)
Request: write access to Source Code

Two notes from team memory:

Note 1 (HR-ish?): role Payroll Specialist, employment type full_time, recommendation write. Comment says full-time employees may have up to write; admin only for owner role. So max is write. Recommend write.

Note 2 (Security): role Payroll Specialist (same as note 1), employment type contractor (looked up in Security DB), security training basic. Recommend read: contractors with basic training max out at read. Requested write exceeds max, so grant read.

Conflict: HR says full-time, Security says contractor. The Security note claims its own database is authoritative for employment type.

Access policy:
- full_time: up to write. Admin only if role owns system. Source Code owned by Engineer role. Payroll Specialist doesn't own Source Code. So max write. Requested write → grant write.
- contractor: read, or write if advanced security training. Basic training → max read. Requested write → grant read (max).

So the decision hinges on which employment type to trust. Note 2 says Security DB is authoritative for employment type. This is a design in this task team: Security agent notes that its DB is authoritative for employment type. Typically in these tasks, the Security database is authoritative. So employment type = contractor, training = basic.

Thus maximum = read. Requested write > read. Grant read.

Let me consider: the notes are from HR agent and Security agent. The Security agent says "Security DB lists E024 as a contractor ... but HR note said full-time, but Security DB is authoritative for employment type." So we should trust Security DB for employment type.

So decision: grant read to Source Code.

Let me submit read with reasoning.
